scenes.name: El sonido de Filadelfia
scenes.book: Funk: The Music, the People, and the Rhythm of the One
scenes.author: Rickey Vincent
scenes.desc: El imperio de Kenny Gamble y Leon Huff, distribuido por CBS: los O’Jays, los Intruders, Billy Paul y Harold Melvin & the Blue Notes con Teddy Pendergrass, sobre la banda de la casa MFSB (Norman Harris, Bobby Eli, Ronnie Baker, Earl Young), la más exitosa de los setenta; su «TSOP» fue la sintonía de Soul Train. Los O’Jays fueron el altavoz del comentario social de Gamble: «Back Stabbers» (1972), Ship Ahoy (1974) con su travesía en un barco negrero, «For the Love of Money» (que el éxito convirtió en música de centro comercial), Survival, Family Reunion. Después de 1976 desapareció el mensaje del soul, y con Gloria Gaynor y Donna Summer la frontera entre el disco, el funk y el soul se borró.
scenes.family: Soul y proto-funk: Stax, Nueva Orleans, Motown

podcast.title: From Drummer to Lead Singer
podcast.body: Teddy Pendergrass made a career-defining move by transitioning from his position as the drummer to the lead singer for Harold Melvin & The Blue Notes, a change that proved instrumental in the group's subsequent success with Philadelphia International Records. "Teddy Pendergrass stepped out from behind the drum kit into the role of lead singer."

podcast.title: Impactful Vocals
podcast.body: Teddy Pendergrass's vocals were recognized as a vital component of the Philly Sound, particularly noted in tracks like "The Love I Lost," where his delivery conveyed a profound sense of pleading, underscoring the critical role of vocalists in PIR's productions. "but those vocals from Teddy, he is practically pleading with whoever it is to come back to him"

podcast.title: Influence on Silk Sonic
podcast.body: Teddy Pendergrass was one of the prominent 70s-style soulmen whose musical tropes and aesthetic were intentionally woven into the fabric of Silk Sonic's debut album, "An Evening with Silk Sonic," as they "play acted the roles of 70s style soulman." "songs bathed in the tropes of Barry White, the Delphanix, Teddy Pendergrass and Aritha Franklin."
